title: Repository hygiene
issueTitle: Phase 0 · 4 — KotlinBottools repository hygiene: .gitignore, gitleaks configuration and CI, README and CHANGELOG
function: KotlinBottools, rewritten onto a fresh repository by unit 3, has no guard against committing its data again: it has no secret scan and no `.github/` directory, its README describes files the rewrite removed from the repository, and it has no changelog. This run adds a root-anchored `.gitignore`, `.gitleaks.toml`, the scan wrapper and a dedicated secret-scan workflow, corrects the README and starts `CHANGELOG.md`, on a branch cut from the rewritten `main`, and merges only once that workflow has passed on its own pull request. Unit 4 of #2, with no version moved.

asked.text: How is the curl-auth-user finding handled so the secret-scan workflow can pass?
options: A (recommended): one scoped allowlist table in .gitleaks.toml, limited to the rule, the one research document and the exact command-substitution text
A': the same, scoped to the rule and the one file only, with no exact text pinned
B: the wrapper and the workflow tolerate default-rule findings and fail only on the custom rules and private-key
C: keep the configuration as designed and merge with the run red; the finding is judged later, before the visibility change
D: a commit-scoped entry for the two commits that carry the line, plus rewording the line on main

plan.detail: Answers: the finding is handled by one scoped allowlist table in .gitleaks.toml, limited to the curl-auth-user rule, the one research document and the exact command-substitution text, with no global allowlist (option A); and the workspace copy of gitleaks.toml follows the committed file at this unit's landing, with the new size and sha256 recorded (option a). The Phase 0 architecture takes dated callouts on sections 5.2, 10, 15 and 16. Research and the plan continue.

Two questions were researched: the workflow on the hosted runner, and the scoped allowlist's semantics at gitleaks 8.30.1. All 42 claims the design rests on hold. With the new configuration the history and the tree scan clean, the canary still fires and the negative controls are still reported. Two points are proved only by the first hosted run: the runner image is moving from Ubuntu 24.04 to 26.04 until 2026-11-19, and the Linux gitleaks binary was not run locally.
